records.title: Change main-engine oil and filter
records.procedure: Warm engine, shut down, drain crankcase, replace lube-oil filter, refill, start and check for leaks, then stop and recheck level.
records.notes: LP668 manual: every 200 operating hours; chart footnote calls for annual maintenance when the hour level is not reached. 668-series lube-oil capacity is 18 qt / 17.0 L. Above 32°F (0°C): SAE 30W single-grade or SAE 15W-40 multigrade; -10°F to 32°F: SAE 10W or 10W-30; below -10°F: SAE 5W or 5W-20. Manual says no crankcase additives or flushing oil.

records.title: Inspect main-engine air cleaner
records.procedure: Inspect element and intake connection. Keep dirt out of the intake; do not run the engine with the cleaner removed.
records.notes: Detailed LP668 service section says inspect the air cleaner every 100 operating hours; replace at 600 hours or yearly.

records.title: Replace primary fuel-filter element
records.procedure: Replace the primary fuel/water-separator element using the installed filter manufacturer’s procedure. If the bowl fills with water, replace both primary and secondary elements immediately.
records.notes: LP668 manual calls for primary element replacement every 200 operating hours or whenever necessary. The exact primary filter model installed on Trickster is not entered here.

records.title: Inspect keel-cooled engine zinc
records.procedure: Drain the expansion tank enough to remove the zinc holder. Remove and clean the zinc. Replace it if more than half consumed. Reinstall with clean threads and good metal-to-metal contact.
records.notes: LP668 manual: check cooling-system zinc electrodes every 200 operating hours; for keel-cooled engines the zinc holder is in the expansion tank.

records.title: Replace main-engine air cleaner
records.procedure: Remove and replace the air-cleaner element, keeping the intake absolutely clean. Inspect the connecting rubber tube and clamps; start and check for leaks.
records.notes: LP668 manual: replace air cleaner every 600 operating hours or yearly, whichever comes first.

records.title: Inspect main-engine V-belt
records.procedure: Inspect belt condition and tension; replace a damaged or deteriorated belt using the engine manual procedure.
records.notes: LP668 service chart lists V-belt condition in the 600-hour/yearly service.

records.title: Replace secondary fuel filter
records.procedure: Shut off fuel, drain/remove the engine-mounted secondary cartridge, install a clean new cartridge, restore fuel and bleed air as required. Check for leaks.
records.notes: LP668 manual: secondary fuel filter every 600 operating hours; 600-hour service is also yearly. Manual identifies secondary cartridge 24-51005.

records.title: Check main-engine fuel injectors
records.procedure: Have injectors checked by a Lugger/Northern Lights dealer or qualified fuel-injection shop.
records.notes: LP668 manual: injector check every 600 operating hours; included in the 600-hour/yearly service.

records.title: Flush main-engine cooling system
records.procedure: With engine stopped and cold, drain and flush the fresh-water cooling circuit using the keel-cooled arrangement, refill with the specified coolant, then run and check for leaks.
records.notes: LP668 manual explicitly calls for cooling-system flush/check for leaks and blockage every 600 operating hours or yearly. Raw-water-pump and heat-exchanger tasks are intentionally omitted for Trickster’s keel-cooled main engine.

records.title: Check main-engine valve clearances
records.procedure: Check/adjust valve clearances with the engine cold using the specified flywheel timing tools/procedure, or have a qualified technician perform the work.
records.notes: LP668 manual: after initial checks, valve clearances recur every 1200 operating hours. Manual values: intake 0.012–0.015 in (0.31–0.38 mm), exhaust 0.016–0.019 in (0.41–0.48 mm), cold.

records.title: Check main-engine fuel-injection pump
records.procedure: Have the fuel-injection pump checked by a qualified diesel fuel-injection service provider.
records.notes: LP668 service schedule lists the fuel-injection pump check at 2400 operating hours.

records.title: Change generator oil and oil filter
records.procedure: Warm generator, shut down, drain oil through the oil-change tube, replace filter, refill, run and check for leaks, stop, wait about 3 minutes and recheck level.
records.notes: M753K manual: every 250 operating hours; oil/filter items are marked for annual maintenance if the hour level is not reached. Capacity with new filter: 3.7 qt / 3.5 L. Above 32°F: SAE 30W or SAE 15W-40; -10°F to 32°F: SAE 10W or 10W-30; below -10°F: SAE 5W or 5W-20. Oil filter: Northern Lights #140516190.

records.title: Inspect generator air cleaner
records.procedure: Inspect the marine air-cleaner element; if dirty, wash in soapy water, rinse and dry thoroughly. Replace if necessary. Keep dirt out of the intake.
records.notes: M753K manual: inspect every 250 operating hours (more often if dusty); item is marked for annual maintenance. Marine air-cleaner element #24-22003.

records.title: Replace generator primary fuel-filter element
records.procedure: Replace the installed primary fuel/water-separator element per its manufacturer instructions. Drain water as needed and check for leaks after service.
records.notes: M753K manual: primary filter element every 500 operating hours or as necessary. Exact Racor model installed on Trickster is not preloaded.

records.title: Replace generator secondary fuel filter
records.procedure: Remove the spin-on secondary filter, oil the new gasket, install and hand-tighten per manual, bleed if needed, run and check for fuel leaks.
records.notes: M753K manual: secondary fuel filter every 500 operating hours; item is marked for annual maintenance. Northern Lights #130336020.

records.title: Inspect generator exhaust elbow
records.procedure: Inspect the exhaust elbow for leakage, corrosion, restriction or deterioration; repair/replace as indicated by inspection.
records.notes: M753K service schedule lists exhaust-elbow inspection every 500 operating hours.

records.title: Service generator air cleaner
records.procedure: Service the marine air-cleaner element; clean if serviceable and replace if necessary. Keep contamination out of the intake.
records.notes: M753K schedule lists air-cleaner element service at 1000 operating hours; air-cleaner item is marked for annual maintenance.

records.title: Check generator valve clearances
records.procedure: With engine cold, check/adjust valve clearances following the M753K procedure or have a qualified technician perform it.
records.notes: M753K manual: every 1000 operating hours; item is marked for annual maintenance. Manual clearance is 0.008 in (0.2 mm) for intake and exhaust.

records.title: Check generator injectors
records.procedure: Have injectors checked by a Northern Lights dealer or local injection-repair station.
records.notes: M753K manual: injector check every 1000 operating hours; item is marked for annual maintenance.

records.title: Replace generator raw-water impeller
records.procedure: Close seacock as appropriate, remove pump cover, remove all old impeller pieces, clean housing, install new impeller and cover gasket, reopen seacock and verify cooling-water discharge/leaks.
records.notes: M753K marine schedule: replace raw-water impeller every 1000 operating hours; item is marked for annual maintenance / as necessary. Manual recommends carrying a spare impeller and cover gasket.

records.title: Check generator fuel-injection pump
records.procedure: Have the injection pump checked by a qualified Northern Lights/diesel fuel-injection service provider.
records.notes: M753K service schedule lists fuel-injection-pump check every 2500 operating hours.

records.title: Flush generator cooling system
records.procedure: With generator cool, drain block/heat-exchanger circuit, flush with clean water until clear, close drains and refill; inspect hoses/connections and leak-check.
records.notes: M753K manual: every 2500 operating hours or 12 months, whichever comes first. Manual coolant specification is 50% water / 50% ethylene-glycol antifreeze.

records.title: Clean generator heat exchanger
records.procedure: Drain cooling circuit, remove heat-exchanger end covers/core, clean tubes, flush and inspect, reassemble, refill and leak-check.
records.notes: M753K marine manual: clean heat exchanger once a year or after 2500 operating hours.

records.title: Change wing-engine oil
records.procedure: Warm engine, shut down, remove old engine oil, refill with specified oil and verify level; run briefly and inspect for leakage.
records.notes: Yanmar 3YM30AE/YM manual: every 150 operating hours or 1 year, whichever comes first. Recommended SAE viscosity: 10W-30 or 15W-40, both usable year-round. API categories listed: CD, CF, CF-4, CI, CI-4; manual says never use CG-4 or CH-4. Exact installed oil quantity is not preloaded because installation/gear configuration has not been verified.

records.title: Replace wing-engine fuel filter
records.procedure: Close fuel supply, replace the engine fuel-filter element cleanly, restore fuel, bleed air as required and check for leakage.
records.notes: Yanmar 3YM30AE periodic schedule: replace fuel-filter element every 250 operating hours or 1 year, whichever comes first.

records.title: Replace wing-engine oil filter
records.procedure: Remove the engine oil-filter element, install the new element per Yanmar instructions, then run and verify oil pressure/leaks and level.
records.notes: Yanmar 3YM30AE periodic schedule: replace engine oil-filter element every 250 operating hours or 1 year, whichever comes first.

records.title: Inspect wing-engine seawater-pump impeller
records.procedure: Inspect the seawater-pump impeller and replace if damaged, cracked, permanently set or otherwise unserviceable; verify seawater flow after reassembly.
records.notes: Yanmar 3YM30AE periodic schedule includes checking/replacing the seawater-pump impeller every 250 operating hours or 1 year. A mandatory replacement also appears in the 1000-hour/4-year service.

records.title: Wing-engine 250-hour / annual inspection service
records.procedure: Drain water/sediment from fuel tank as applicable; clean intake silencer; clean/check exhaust-water mixing elbow; adjust alternator V-ribbed belt; inspect wiring connectors. Address defects found.
records.notes: These items are listed in the Yanmar 3YM30AE 250-operating-hour / 1-year maintenance group. Marine-gear oil is deliberately excluded because Trickster’s installed gear model has not been verified.

records.title: Wing-engine 1000-hour / 4-year major service
records.procedure: Major service: replace seawater-pump impeller; clean/check seawater passages; inspect diaphragm assembly; replace alternator belt; check/adjust valve clearance and remote-control cables; check propeller-shaft alignment and major fasteners. Have injection timing and injector spray pattern checked by an authorized Yanmar dealer/service provider.
records.notes: Yanmar 3YM30AE periodic schedule: every 1000 operating hours or 4 years, whichever comes first. This task groups the verified major-service items to keep the log manageable.

records.title: Replace/inspect bow-thruster anode
records.procedure: At seasonal service/haulout, inspect the sacrificial anode; replace before the season or when about half consumed. Use thread-lock/sealant on the retaining screw and do not paint the anode.
records.notes: SP155 TC manual: replace the zinc anode before every season or when about half gone. Current Sleipner documentation lists zinc 20 1180 and aluminum-alloy 20 1180A as SP155-compatible anodes. Twelve months is used here to represent the manufacturer’s once-per-season instruction.

records.title: Seasonal bow-thruster gearhouse/propeller service
records.procedure: At haulout, check gear-oil quality, propeller security/free rotation, gearhouse/propeller fouling and electrical/mechanical condition. Antifoul gearhouse/propeller as appropriate, but never paint the anode, seals or propeller shafts.
records.notes: SP155 TC manual: check gear-oil quality whenever the boat is out of the water and clean/antifoul propeller and gearhouse before every season.

records.title: Change bow-thruster gear oil
records.procedure: Drain/change gear oil per SP155 TC procedure and refill reservoir/gearhouse. Confirm oil can flow freely from the reservoir to the gearhouse and check for leakage.
records.notes: SP155 TC manual: change gear oil a minimum of every second year. Specified lubricant: EP90 gear oil; the reservoir must always contain oil.

records.title: Replace/inspect stern-thruster anode
records.procedure: At seasonal service/haulout, inspect the sacrificial anode; replace before the season or when about half consumed. Use thread-lock/sealant on the retaining screw and do not paint the anode.
records.notes: SP155 TC manual: replace the zinc anode before every season or when about half gone. Current Sleipner documentation lists zinc 20 1180 and aluminum-alloy 20 1180A as SP155-compatible anodes. Twelve months is used here to represent the manufacturer’s once-per-season instruction.

records.title: Seasonal stern-thruster gearhouse/propeller service
records.procedure: At haulout, check gear-oil quality, propeller security/free rotation, gearhouse/propeller fouling and electrical/mechanical condition. Antifoul gearhouse/propeller as appropriate, but never paint the anode, seals or propeller shafts.
records.notes: SP155 TC manual: check gear-oil quality whenever the boat is out of the water and clean/antifoul propeller and gearhouse before every season.

records.title: Change stern-thruster gear oil
records.procedure: Drain/change gear oil per SP155 TC procedure and refill reservoir/gearhouse. Confirm oil can flow freely from the reservoir to the gearhouse and check for leakage.
records.notes: SP155 TC manual: change gear oil a minimum of every second year. Specified lubricant: EP90 gear oil; the reservoir must always contain oil.

records.title: Annual stabilizer inspection/service
records.procedure: Check fin-actuator bonding; verify cooling-water supply and normal temperature; check pressure-filter indicator; inspect pumps/reservoir/valves/cylinder rods, hoses and piping for leakage/damage; check fin-actuator mounting fasteners and lubricate trunnion/rod-end areas; perform centering and movement checks.
records.notes: Naiad 162-254 owner handbook lists these items under yearly routine maintenance. Heat-exchanger zinc inspection is not included because the handbook states zinc-equipped heat exchangers are system-dependent and Trickster’s exact heat-exchanger configuration has not been verified.

records.title: Change stabilizer reservoir oil
records.procedure: Drain reservoir oil, reinstall drain plug without overtightening, and refill through a clean funnel and disposable paper strainer using the correct Naiad-approved oil for the installed system.
records.notes: Naiad 162-254 handbook: every 3 years or 4000 operating hours. No stabilizer-hour meter is preloaded because one has not been verified on Trickster; add a 4000-hour meter trigger if reliable stabilizer operating hours become available.

records.title: Replace stabilizer lower shaft seals
records.procedure: Schedule at haulout. Center and positively lock fin actuators before service. Replace lower shaft seals with genuine Naiad seals following the handbook/service procedure.
records.notes: Naiad 162-254 handbook: replace lower seals every 3 years or 4000 operating hours, more frequently if fin shafts are not cycled at least twice per month. No unverified stabilizer-hour meter has been created.

records.title: Quarterly windlass clean/lubricate service
records.procedure: Disassemble above-deck components to the deckplate, clean and inspect, grease components—especially clutch-cone surfaces—then reassemble. Inspect below-deck components for corrosion and protect as needed.
records.notes: Maxwell 2200 VWC manual: every 3 months. Use lithium-complex-base waterproof grease, consistency No. 2. Never mix incompatible greases.

records.title: Annual windlass motor/drainage service
records.procedure: Perform quarterly service, remove gearbox/spacer tube/motor as directed, flush drainage slots clear of debris, and service the DC motor.
records.notes: Maxwell 2200 VWC manual: every year in addition to the three-month service.

records.title: Three-year windlass gearbox service
records.procedure: Perform annual service, remove spacer tube, clean mating faces, drain gearbox, replace seals, flush if appropriate, then fill gearbox completely with new specified oil.
records.notes: Maxwell 2200 VWC manual: every 3 years. Gearbox lubricant: ISO 3448 VG 320. Approximate fill: 800 mL / 27 fl oz. Never mix oil types.

records.title: Quarterly house-battery inspection
records.procedure: Inspect each terminal for corrosion; clean/neutralize/dry and protect if needed. Check connections for looseness. With bank on float charge, record system float voltage, each battery voltage and ambient temperature.
records.notes: Lifeline AGM Technical Manual Rev. G recommends quarterly terminal inspection and float-voltage/individual-battery/temperature records. AGM batteries do not require electrolyte adjustment. Exact terminal hardware is not verified, so no torque value is entered.

records.title: Annual house-battery capacity/charging-system test
records.procedure: Run a full charge cycle and record charger current, absorption/float/ripple voltage, each battery voltage and ambient temperature. Perform a controlled capacity discharge test, record run time/Ah/load/end voltage, then recharge fully as soon as possible.
records.notes: Lifeline AGM Technical Manual Rev. G recommends this yearly service. No invented capacity result or replacement threshold is preloaded.

records.title: Initial 50h: drain wing-engine fuel tank
records.procedure: Drain water and sediment from the fuel tank as specified by Yanmar's initial 50-hour maintenance. Use an approved container and stop when fuel is clean/free of sediment. Exact Trickster tank/drain arrangement should be confirmed before opening anything.

source.reference: Yanmar YM Series Operation Manual, 2025.02, sections 'New Engine Break-In' and 'After Initial 50 Hours of Operation'

records.notes: Verified initial 50-hour maintenance item from the Yanmar YM Series Operation Manual.

records.title: Initial 50h: change Yanmar engine oil and filter
records.procedure: Initial break-in oil service. Change engine oil while warm and replace the engine-oil filter element. Use the oil specification already recorded for the 3YM30AE in this dataset/manufacturer manual.

source.reference: Yanmar YM Series Operation Manual, 2025.02, sections 'New Engine Break-In' and 'After Initial 50 Hours of Operation'

records.title: Initial 50h: service Yanmar marine gear oil/filter
records.procedure: Yanmar calls for changing marine-gear oil and replacing the marine-gear oil filter if equipped at the initial 50 hours. The installed marine-gear model on Trickster has not been verified here, so confirm its model/manual, oil specification, capacity, and whether a filter is fitted before servicing.

records.title: Initial 50h: check/adjust Yanmar alternator belt tension
records.procedure: Check and adjust the alternator V-ribbed belt tension per the Yanmar YM Series manual. Inspect the belt for damage while checking tension.

source.reference: Yanmar YM Series Operation Manual, 2025.02, sections 'New Engine Break-In' and 'After Initial 50 Hours of Operation'

records.title: Initial 50h: inspect/adjust Yanmar valve clearance
records.procedure: Inspect and adjust intake/exhaust valve clearance as specified for the initial 50-hour service. This is precision engine work; follow the Yanmar procedure/specification rather than using a generic clearance.

source.reference: Yanmar YM Series Operation Manual, 2025.02, sections 'New Engine Break-In' and 'After Initial 50 Hours of Operation'

records.title: Initial 50h: check/adjust Yanmar remote-control cables
records.procedure: Check and adjust the remote-control cables so shift/throttle controls move correctly through their intended positions. Follow the Yanmar procedure for the installed control arrangement.

source.reference: Yanmar YM Series Operation Manual, 2025.02, sections 'New Engine Break-In' and 'After Initial 50 Hours of Operation'

records.title: Initial 50h: check wing propeller-shaft alignment
records.procedure: Yanmar specifies checking and adjusting propeller-shaft alignment after the first 50 hours because flexible engine mounts may settle during initial operation. Yanmar notes this requires specialized knowledge/techniques; use a qualified marine technician if appropriate.
